Addressed:

1. The wall test now samples inside each segment. A vertex probe cannot remove the credit for a legal inside corner.
   Tests: `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_an_l_shaped_boss_stays_clean` and `a_no_pick_chamfer_on_a_rectangular_pocket_stays_clean`.
   Both tests failed with the old code and passed with the fix. The L-shaped boss reproduced the reported 1,141-cell gouge.
   All five `chamfer_modelled_edge` tests passed. The test for an unsafe tip inside the part still rejects the program.
2. The decision record now specifies the 0.05 mm facet-top probe in `sim::stock_sim::wall_anchor`.
   Focused text assertions failed on the old record and passed on the corrected record.
   The gate-map note now names `wall_anchor::on_walls`.

Validation: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 215 steps, with zero failures.
Clippy passed for motion, sim, and app, with all targets and warnings denied.

New head: `b521da7ef94bb0907c2050b0e832109db5cd1f22`.
Please review this head again. The PR remains a draft.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b521da7ef94bb0907c2050b0e832109db5cd1f22 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Review tier: SAFETY. The PR changes 2D Chamfer paths and gouge checks.

Both blocking findings from the review of `49c268ba7384a04d2b551435411d5b4b44661f17` are resolved.

- The wall test samples segment interiors. The L-shaped boss and rectangular pocket keep their edge-break credit.
- The decision record now specifies the 0.05 mm facet-top probe in `wall_anchor`. The test's Gate map also names this module.
- The generator places the tip on the wall at the corner depth. The unsafe inward tip remains a blocking gouge.
- The new modules have provenance comments. I found no blocking violation of the current upstream `AGENTS.md`.
- No golden files, UI files, dependencies, build scripts or workflow files changed.

Local build and test results:

The reviewer repeated these mutations locally:

1. Ride the top section again: both tip-position tests failed. The tip stayed at `(19,-9,9)` or `(19,-9,9.5)`.
2. Disable the wall filter: the gouge test failed with `a cone tip inside the part posted`.
3. Restore vertex sampling: both corner tests failed. The boss reported 1141 gouged cells; the pocket reported 664. Each reported a worst gouge of 0.94 mm.

All temporary changes were restored. All five chamfer regression tests passed again. The worktree had no remaining edits.

Requested before merge: none.

Nonblocking limitation: a modelled square pocket bevel can still give a named refusal from the outline matcher.
The local probe used a mouth at ±11 mm and Z10, with a wall rim at ±10 mm and Z9.
Generation refused it with the location and advice to pick the edges. It did not produce an unsafe path.
Issue #2435 explicitly permits a named refusal, so this result does not block this fix.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Read-only safety-floor review (Opus, diff only, not built) of head b521da7ef94bb0907c2050b0e832109db5cd1f22.

Verdict: findings (no blocker, three notes)

What I checked:
- The generator change in `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs` and `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`.
- The verify change in `crates/app/src/stock_sim_breaks.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs` and `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/wall_anchor.rs`.
- The new tests and the decision record.

Safety result:
- The verify change only removes credit. A dropped record makes the verdict stricter, never looser. No refusal or safety check is removed or weakened.
- A NaN or infinite value in `walled` makes the comparison false. The record is then dropped, so the result is stricter. `Tops::ix`/`iy` clamp the index, and `buckets.get` / `facets.get` are checked. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` is outside tests.
- On a vertical wall the top loop is ridden unchanged (`gap <= SAME_EDGE`). Posted G-code changes only on a model with a modelled bevel. The PR body states this.
- A top loop with no wall within the width is refused by name with the spot. This is correct.
- The tests compare real geometry: the tip positions on the wall, the gate result, and a reverted ride that must give a gouge. The PR body says each test was mutation-checked.

Findings:

1. note - `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`, `ride_loops`, the one-sided `gap` match. The match only measures the top loop to the wall loop. A wall loop at the corner depth can contain an outline that is not under a top edge. Example: a bevelled boss with a rib or ledge attached, whose top is between `corner_z` and the top plane. The corner section merges the boss wall and the rib wall into one loop. The top loop matches it (gap about the width), and the ride then follows the rib wall too. The cone then chamfers the rib's top edge, which the user did not ask for. The record edge is at `top_z`, and `credit_breaks` credits columns under a model top lower than the edge, so verify credits this cut and does not report it. This contradicts the decision record ("a lower ledge ... is not ridden"). It is not a regression: before this PR the same part got a V inside the bevel, also credited. Recommendation: also check the reverse gap (wall loop to top loop, with a slack for the mitred corner, for example `width * sqrt(2)` plus slack), or refuse by name when the reverse gap is too large. Add a test with a bevelled boss and an attached lower rib.

2. note - same function. Two top loops can match the same wall loop (two bevelled islands that merge at the corner depth). The wall loop is then pushed two times. `Region::new` can refuse this (safe), or the ride can run two times on one loop. No test pins this case. Recommendation: refuse by name when one wall loop matches more than one top loop, or ride it only one time.

3. note - `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs`, the new `Chamfer2D` arm. `corner_z = z - width * tan(angle)` is used in `section(...)` before `ride_loops` checks that `corner_z` is finite. If the angle is not validated to be inside (0, 90) degrees when the command is created, `section` gets a NaN or very large Z. I did not read `section` to see what it does with that value. Recommendation: check `corner_z.is_finite()` before the second `section` call.

Test coverage notes (no action needed for merge):
- No test pins a pocket rim with a modelled bevel (the wall loop inside the top loop). The pocket test uses vertical walls only.
- The tilted (3+2) frame is not tested. The PR body states this.

What I did not check:
- I did not build or run any test. I did not read the full `section` function or the chamfer kernel beyond its `EdgeBreak` construction.
- I did not check the QA part results in the PR body.
- I did not check run time of `on_walls` on large models. Each record scans all facets one time, which is linear in the facet count for each record.
